content.title: How does the World Baseball Classic work? See schedule, format, rules
content.text: March 6, 2026, 5:01 a.m. ETTwenty teams from across the globe are playing in the 2026 World Baseball Classic. Games began March 4 with the championship set for March 17 in Miami.Japan is the reigning WBC champion, having beaten the United States 3-2 in the 2023 final. The Samurai have won three of the five tournament titles.Teams are divided into five-team pools. The two teams with the best records in each of the four pools will advance to the single-elimination knockoff stages.The ABS system that automated balls and strikes will not be used in the WBC. Pitchers are limited to the amount of pitches they can throw per game and have mandated rest between appearances.Baseball fans were ecstatic in 2023 for the World Baseball Classic. The best event in the tournament's history was capped by an instant classic, when Shohei Ohtani struck out then-Angels teammate Mike Trout to clinch Japan's win over Team USA in front of a raucous Miami crowd.What will the WBC have in store in 2026? The tournament is a little different this time around, though once again the semifinals and championship will take place at the Miami Marlins' stadium. Only one of the four round-robin pools are taking place outside the United States, with Tokyo kicking off the competition. The other three — housed in Miami, Houston and San Juan, Puerto Rico — begin play March 6.Nations taking part range from perennial MLB funnels like Venezuela and Korea to Caribbean stalwarts Cuba and the Dominican Republic, as well as some countries fielding major-leaguers who may or may not have ever been to said country (looking at Aaron Nola on Italy and Harrison Bader on Israel). MLB might be implementing challenges on balls and strikes this year, but in the WBC, it's still all up to the umpires.Watch select World Baseball Classic games live on FuboThe United States enters as favorites with a star-packed lineup featuring reigning AL MVP Aaron Judge and both of last year's Cy Young winners, Paul Skenes and Tarik Skubal. Ohtani and Dodgers teammate Yoshinobu Yamamoto will be back for Japan, while the Dominican Republic's similarly loaded roster includes Juan Soto, Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and Julio Rodriguez. Not all of the world's best players will be on hand, as some stars are being kept out for insurance purposes. Puerto Rico, one of the perennial contenders to win it all, was especially hit hard with eight players missing out, including Francisco Lindor and Carlos Correa.With the WBC now fully underway, here's everything fans need to know about the tournament, including the teams involved, schedule, format, special rules and how to watch.What is the World Baseball Classic?Baseball's answer to the FIFA World Cup, the World Baseball Classic is a global tournament that pits national teams against each other in a two-week tournament to determine the best in the world. It began in 2006 and has taken place every three to four years, skipping the 2021 tournament because of the COVID pandemic.When does the World Baseball Classic begin?The 2026 WBC got underway late March 4 ... well, it was in the United States, anyway. Pool C games are being played in Tokyo, Japan, where the opener took place March 5. The other sites begin play Friday, March 6. Here's where the U.S. games will take place. Keep scrolling to see which teams are playing in each pool.Pool A: Hiram Bithorn Stadium, San Juan, Puerto RicoPool B: Daikan Park, Houston, TexasPool D: LoanDepot Park, Miami, FloridaWBC formatEach team plays a minimum of four nine-inning games, one against each member of their pool. The two teams with the best record in each pool will advance to the single-elimination quarterfinals March 13-14 in either Miami or Houston. The winners will gather in Miami for the semifinals March 15-16, then the championship game March 17.Tiebreakers could determine which team wins a pool or which one moves on to the knockout stages. Here's the WBC tiebreaker policy:Head-to-head resultsFewest runs allowed divided by outs recorded in games between tied teamsFewest earned runs allowed divided by outs recorded in games between tied teamsHighest batting average in games between tied teamsDrawing of lotsWorld Baseball Classic rulesThe WBC will play mostly by MLB rules. Here's a look at some of the changes for the 2026 tournament:Pitch clock: The MLB pitch clock will be in effect. Pitchers have 15 seconds to deliver a pitch with the bases empty and 18 seconds with runners on base; if they don't, the umpire will award a ball. Batters must be ready in the box at 8 seconds or be given a strike.ABS: The Automatic Ball-Strike System will not be used, meaning balls and strikes are solely up to the umpire.Pitch counts: To protect their arms for the club season, pitchers may not throw more than 65 pitches in a first-round game, 80 pitches in the knockout stages and 95 pitches in the championship game, except to complete an at-bat.Pitcher limitations: A pitcher who throws 50 or more pitches in a game must be given four days' rest. Throwing 30 pitches requires one day's rest, as does pitching on consecutive days.Mercy rule: First-round and quarterfinal games will end if a team is ahead by 10 runs after seven innings or 15 runs after five innings. The semifinals and championship games will complete all nine innings regardless of score.Where to watch WBC 2026All World Baseball Classic games will be broadcast on the Fox family of networks. Most will air on Fox, FS1 and FS2, and those games can be streamed live on Fubo, which offers a free trial for new subscribers. Some games will be available only via streaming on either Tubi or the Fox One app, which can be bundled into the ESPN Unlimited package.
